posts.name: Ameena
posts.cooked:
Alrighty, we just finished our first online game! It was playe over Skype, text-chat only. Players were as follows…

Myself, playing Ra

Mezike, playing Fanatic

Matchstickman, playing Legacy

We fought Baron Blade in Megalopolis

Technically this was a pretty short game, but it took at least an hour or so because of the nature of playing such a thing over the Internet ;). There were no huge disasters, really. We had a bit of a mildly annoying phase where we had Hostage Situation come up (can't play cards), followed by another Hostage Situation right after we got rid of the first one, and then the following turn it was replaced by Paparazzi on the Scene (can't use powers). So that slowed us down a bit. I think Blade got seven cards into his trash before we flipped him. Might have been eight, but either way we had a while to go before things started looking dodgy :). By this point he also had two Living Force Fields (+1 damage soak) in play, which was slightly annoying but with Legacy's buffs, plus a Rooftop Combat followed closely by a Cramped Quarters Combat (both +1 damage, okay so we didn't have both  out at once), it didn't impact us too greatly. Eventually I got the killing blow. I ended the game on 10hp, and I think both Legacy and Fanatic had 16. Great fun was had by all and we intend to do it again some time!

posts.name: Matchstickman

Text was very slow, it took us about 90 minutes to play it... but it was still fun and it easier to keep track of HP and buffs etc as it was all right there in the chat log. I tried to keep in character for the game, which is easier over text.

The decks? Yeah I believe someone only has EE but we wanted to try a basic game because it was the first time we were playing this way, we didn't even play advanced as someone has not played an advanced game, ever(!).

Having played both voice and text I prefer voice, no real slow down in the action, easier to get your intent across to people and more sense of actually playing together but I don't think I'd turn down a game just because it was over text.

posts.name: Mezike
posts.cooked:
There was some good characterisation all the way through which the text really brought out, and keeping track of everything was easy and clear, at the cost of a slower game. The game was relaxed and I felt like I had time to get my cards and effects sorted without keeping everybody hanging on plus, on a personal note, I could play without turning my wife into a Sentinels widow, the value of which mustn't be underestimated

 

We went core as we wanted to keep things as simple as possible for the first go round, it's a familiar groove with a set up that most of us have probably played at some point so there were less surprises (expect for my terrible shuffling of the environment deck.) Now that we've made it work I think something more adventurous will be on the slate for next time.

 

In any case it was fun all the way through and the time flew by; I was about to suggest a second game when I looked at the time and couldn't believe that 90 mins had passed! We had quite a bit of chat before and after too which was nice, and a bit of in-character silliness at the end which I doubt would have worked as well in real life.

 

Some suggestions for running text based games would be to post your HP and ongoing effects at the end of your turn, and to name the next character as a way of passing play. We kept this up most of the time and it really helped to get a reminder of what buffs were active and who had the most/least HP (which informed my play as Fanatic a couple of times.) Once or twice we jumped in over each other, no big deal though and no worse than overtalk in a conference call. We didn't have a great deal of strategising to get through but that was probably more to do with the chosen decks than anything else.

 

All in all I think it was a success and I am looking forward to the next one. I'd like to try a voice based game, unfortunately my headset doesn't work with my tablet either so I'll probably be stuck with text until I can find a replacement. Buying a headset just to play Sentinels would be a difficult sell for me, having just broken my wallet on the kickstarter!

posts.cooked:
Here I am, finally online...though I won't be on Skype tonight, or tomorrow, as I'm not at home right now. I won't be on Skype till I get home on Sunday evening.

But here's what happened in that game I played with Mezike last night...

It was about half ten when we decuded to play, though it took us a while to actually start playing, and we didn't finish till about 1am. Yeah, long game but very fun ;). So, we decided to go up against the MAtriarch, as Mezike hadn't played against her yet. He decided he'd play two heroes, so there'd be three heroes in total, and went with Expatriette and Tempest. I chose Mr Fixer, in the hopes of getting out Driving Mantis style in order to redirect any Fowl-destruction damage that I might be dealt. Finally, we decided on the environment, choosing the Tomb of Anubis with the theory that the traps would help us get rid of the Matriarch's stuff.

So, Tempest was able to reliably clear birdies with Squall on more than one occasion. Expatriette achieved the same with her Sub-Machine Gun a few times to. We had both cohorts out at one point, which was annoying, but managed to get rid of them eventually. I'd started with a Harmony carde in-hand but never actually played it. I also started with Grease Monkey Fist style, and played it (more to just get a style into play than because I wanted that particular style), only to lose it to a Horrid Cacophony on the Matriarch's next turn :P. That was the only style card I saw during the whole game but that was okay. I actually didn't do very much damage, but was able to be effective nevertheless. We never took any damage from Fowl directly, but we did from destroying them. Also, one or two environmental traps hit us on a couple of occasions. However, after losing quite a lot of hp over a couple of turns, we finally stopped at around the 10hp mark. Because I'd drawn a Grease Gun. I played this, to stop all the bad guys doing damage (except the traps, which aren't targets so are unaffected by the Grease Gun), which meant Expatriette (whose turn was after mine) could gun down all the birdies with no repercussions. On the following turn, of course, my Grease Gun was destroyed, so I just played the Salvage Yard card I had in my hand and got it back again, playing it again the following turn. I also then drew a second Grease Gun, so played that on the turn after. On Tempest's next turn, he got one of my Grease Guns out of the trash with a Reclaim from the Deep, so I drew that on my next turn. The turn after that, however, I didn't bother playing it because by this time Tempest and Expatriette had whittled down the Matriarch to 5hp so I used Strike to do her two damage (I had a Pipe Wrench out). Expatriette finished things off - she already had Pride in play (and had done for most of the game), so on the final turn she played a Quick Draw to locate Prejudice as well, and unleashed both guns into the Matriarch's face. BOOM.

Who says Mr Fixer and Expatriette aren't much good? ;) Expatriette probably did the most damage, while Mr Fixer, I'm certain, saved everyone from dying with the multiple Grease Gun uses :). We ended the game with Mr Fixer on 10hp, Tempest on 9hp, and Expatriette on 8hp. And we had a good time, even if we were both half asleep by the end :D. Things looked rather worrying quite early on, when there were about a million birds out and we had no protection, but we managed to deal with it and ended up kicking some feathery arse :D.

Text-based games over Skype are a bit slow, yes, but that doesn't make them any less fun :D.

That first game was great, a classic and efficient villain dismantling. The second was a bit more sloppy and ran on for quite a bit. Memo to self not to start a game past 10pm with a slow building team! 

One thing we discussed was the lack of 'table vision' where you can't see everything that is in play, how this impacts on strategy and requires additional dialogue as you have to ask more questions of the other players. Although this is a major contributor to slowing the game down I quite like the way it feels like a group of individuals coming together, you know what they are capable of but never 100% on what their current active abilities are. It was fun to see us making a few sub optimal decisions, then working things out after all, which was as enjoyable a challenge as when we fixed a team strategy and played it out effectively.

Vassal may have helped but is limited. Is there any mileage in a Vassal module that has the card names but no text, and limited artwork? i.e. the same base picture on every card with the card name, also making the cards smaller. In this way it would be possible to have the whole game manageable in Vassal whilst still requiring players to own a copy, it would purely be a module for tracking game state in online games. Just a thought, or we could investigate live document sharing so HP and game effects re more easily visible.

posts.name: Ronway
posts.cooked:
Mechanically Absolute Zero needs at least two cards to become extremely effect, those cards are Null-Point Callibration Unit (Whenever he is dealt Cold damage, he gets healed by that much instead) and Isothermic Transducer (Whenever he is dealt fire damage he also deals 1 target that much cold damage) so basically I went a little bit without the Transducer, so I was basically just healing myself for the first, probably 4/5 rounds. A lot of his cards has effects that does something then deals himself either cold or fire damage, sometimes even both. After getting those two there are a lot of options to choose from.

 

In the case of when I played HoarFire, I had originally stated that I would be full health on my turn, which I then switched to saying I will be the lowest. HoarFire deals 1 targer 2 cold damage. A second target 2 fire damage. Then himself 1 cold and 1 fire damage. Initially I was going to use the cold damage on myself, thus healing, and the fire damage to Voss. Then of course I would take the 1 cold and fire, which I would be able to hit Voss for cold damage again since I was hit by fire. But after remembering that Voss deals fire to the lowest, I decided it would be much more beneificial to be the lowest, so I then used the cold damage on Voss, hit myself with the fire damage, thus once again hitting Voss, followed by me dealing myself 1 cold and 1 fire damage and hitting Voss with more cold damage since I was once again hit by fire.

 

The scary thing is that the example I did was only one card. So many cards work together in his deck that cause so much going on in a single turn that he sometimes will need to take the time to think things out.

 

Themetically I like to think AZ's slow build is becausehe  doesn't care what is going on until the something happens that effects him toa  great deal. In our game it seems to be the defeat of Visionary since the turn following that is when I actually did damage, and not just a little bit of damage, a whole whopping 17 points worth.
